name: Boac Cathedral
description: Perched on a hilltop fortress in Mataas na Bayan since 1792, the Immaculate Conception Cathedral Parish is Marinduque's spiritual seat and a declared Important Cultural Property.
howToGetThere: Take a jeepney from Balanacan Port to Boac town proper (~35 min), then walk uphill behind Boac Plaza or ride a tricycle straight to the parish gate.
bestTime: Early morning daylight for limestone photography, late-afternoon breeze, Sunday Mass, or Holy Week observances.
tips: Dress modestly for church interiors and spare 20 minutes to stroll the heritage ancestral houses and museum downhill around Boac Centro.

name: Luzon Datum of 1911
estimatedCost: Free site · TODO: check view fee
highlights: 360° sea views on Mt. Mataas crest
description: Station Balanacan sits atop Mt. Mataas in Brgy. Hinanggayon—the exact historical origin point established in 1911 from which geodetic surveys across the Philippines were referenced.
howToGetThere: From Balanacan Port or Mogpog town proper, hire a tricycle or habal-habal up the coastal ridge road to Brgy. Hinanggayon, then climb the 468 concrete steps to the summit obelisk.
bestTime: Clear dry-season mornings or late afternoons before sunset across Tayabas Bay.
tips: Bring cold water and sun protection—the 468-step staircase rises steeply across exposed coastal ridge slopes above Balanacan Bay.
photoCredit: Photo: T3n60 (Balanacan View Deck) · Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

name: Maniwaya Island
description: Laid-back northeast outer island lined with long pale beaches, calm reef shallows, and seaside homestays serving as the classic launch point to Palad Sandbar.
howToGetThere: Take a van to Santa Cruz Centro (~1.5 hours from Boac), tricycle 10–15 min to Buyabod Port (not Balanacan Port), and board a 30–45 min boat (TODO: confirm daily public boat schedule).
bestTime: March to May calm summer months; arrive by early morning to catch regular public bangka departures.
tips: Bring sufficient PHP cash—there are no ATMs on Maniwaya Island, and local power or cellular signal can dip intermittently.

name: Palad Sandbar
highlights: Tidal arc of powdery coral sand
description: An ephemeral crescent of bright white sand that rises from turquoise coral flats northeast of Maniwaya Island when tides recede. TODO: verify exact low-tide bar GPS on site.
howToGetThere: Join a ~20–30 min boat hop from Maniwaya Island resorts or charter an outrigger bangka directly from Buyabod Port in Santa Cruz.
bestTime: Morning low-tide windows between March and May (always check daily tide tables before departure).
tips: Zero trees or permanent huts stand on the exposed sandbar—pack wide-brim hats, reef-safe sunscreen, water, and aqua shoes.

name: Poctoy White Beach
description: A sweeping kilometer-long curve of fine cream-white coral sand fringed by coconut palms, facing clear cobalt waters and the volcanic silhouette of Mt. Malindig.
howToGetThere: Ride a van or jeepney from Balanacan Port or Boac south-east to Torrijos Centro (~1.5–2 hours), then hop a 5-minute tricycle east to Brgy. Poctoy shoreline.
bestTime: Dry-season weekdays and golden sunrise mornings from December through May.
tips: Bring cash for beachfront picnic cottages or local carinderias nearby; northeast habagat/amihan gusts can kick up gentle surf outside summer.

name: Mt. Malindig
estimatedCost: Guide req. · TODO: verify brgy. fee
description: Marinduque's towering dormant stratovolcano and wildlife sanctuary crowning the southern peninsula, rewarded with sweeping ridge vistas across southern Luzon and Mindoro.
howToGetThere: Travel to Buenavista Centro and ride a tricycle inland to the Brgy. Sihi jump-off to register at the barangay hall and hire a mandatory local trail guide.
bestTime: Pre-dawn dry-season hikes (November to May); trails frequently close during heavy monsoon rains or slippery fog.
tips: Start early with at least 2 L of water, trail snacks, rain shell, and proper lugged footwear—the final cloud-forest slopes stay damp year-round.

name: Tres Reyes Islands
description: A trio of forested limestone islets—Gaspar, Melchor, and Baltazar—rising off Gasan's southwest coast, known for quiet white coves and steep reef walls.
howToGetThere: Ride a tricycle south from Gasan Centro to Brgy. Pinggan dock (~10 min), then charter a 30–45 min outrigger bangka to Gaspar Island.
bestTime: November to May calm morning seas; avoid southwest monsoon swells from June to October.
tips: Gaspar Island hosts the main beach landing while Melchor and Baltazar suit cliff-viewing and drift snorkeling—carry own snorkel gear and drinking water.

name: Our Lady of Biglang Awa Shrine
highlights: Short seaside walk from port gate
description: A monumental coastal shrine standing watch over the narrow turquoise channel of Balanacan Harbor, welcoming inbound RORO ferries from Lucena like a maritime beacon.
howToGetThere: Walk ~5–10 minutes east along the causeway promenade directly outside Balanacan Port terminal in Brgy. Balanacan, Mogpog.
bestTime: Golden hour before sunset or right as RORO ferries glide across the sheltered cove.
tips: Ideal first or final stop while waiting for Balanacan ferry boarding—careful on windy stairways beside the sea wall.

name: Paadjao Cascades
description: Tucked inside a lush bamboo-and-fern gorge in Brgy. Bocboc, Paadjao Cascades plunges roughly 100 feet across dark basalt ledges into a natural emerald plunge pool.
howToGetThere: Ride a tricycle or jeepney from Mogpog or Boac inland toward Brgy. Bocboc (~30 min), then follow the short shaded concrete footpath to the basin (TODO: verify trailhead GPS).
bestTime: Weekday mornings between November and May, or soon after moderate rains when flow peaks cleanly.
tips: Boulders around the lower pool turn slick with moss—wear grippy sandals or water shoes and pack light dry snacks.

name: Bulusukan Falls
description: Secluded inland waterfall nestled in Sitio Bahay-Igat, Brgy. Maybo south of Boac proper, framed by mossy boulders and tall tropical canopy.
howToGetThere: Hire a tricycle south from Boac Centro along the river valley road to Brgy. Maybo (~25–30 min), register locally, and walk ~15–20 min upstream along the rocky riverbed.
bestTime: Morning sunlight filtering into the gorge during cool dry months (January to May).
tips: Bring sturdy aqua shoes for wet river crossings and pack out all trash; cellular service drops inside the valley.

name: Bathala Caves
description: A historic limestone karst network of chambers set in the wooded foothills of Sitio Bathala, famous for high vaulted galleries, bat roosts, and limestone formations. TODO: verify exact cave trailhead GPS in Brgy. Ipil.
howToGetThere: Ride a tricycle ~10 km north from Santa Cruz Centro to Brgy. Ipil, register at the barangay post, and hire an accredited local guide for the steep hill ascent.
bestTime: Dry-season mornings from November to May; inner chambers become muddy during heavy downpours.
tips: Pack high-traction shoes, a strong headlamp or flashlight, bottled water, and avoid touching delicate damp speleothems.

name: Battle of Pulang Lupa Shrine
description: Ridge sanctuary atop Mt. Bintakay in Brgy. Bolo marking the September 13, 1900 Battle of Pulang Lupa—a decisive Filipino victory led by Lt. Col. Maximo Abad during the Philippine–American War.
howToGetThere: From Torrijos town proper, hire a tricycle or motorcycle uphill northwest via Brgy. Bolo ridge road (~15–20 min) to the memorial park gate.
bestTime: Early morning or late afternoon for cool mountain breezes and clear views down toward Poctoy coast.
tips: Combine easily in a half-day Torrijos loop alongside Poctoy White Beach; read the carved NHI plaque recounting the 1900 ambush.
photoCredit: Photo: Josh Lim / Eugene Alvin Villar · Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

name: Malbog Sulfuric Spring
description: Geothermal mineral pools (~36–40°C) fed by volcanic springs along Mt. Malindig's southern foothills, tucked beneath breezy rain-tree canopy in Brgy. Malbog.
howToGetThere: Take a coastal jeepney to Buenavista Centro (~1 hour south of Boac) and ride a 10-minute tricycle inland to Brgy. Malbog.
bestTime: Cool weekday mornings between December and February (typically ~6 AM–5 PM; TODO: confirm resort operating hours).
tips: Remove silver rings, necklaces, and watches before dipping—the natural sulfur compounds tarnish sterling silver within minutes.

name: Talao Caves
estimatedCost: Guide fee · TODO: verify brgy. rate
description: A twelve-chamber karst cave complex carved into coastal hills of Brgy. Tiguion overlooking Gasan, celebrated for hanging limestone formations and sunlit cavern windows. TODO: verify exact cave trailhead GPS in Brgy. Tiguion.
howToGetThere: Take a tricycle ~15 min northeast from Gasan Centro into Brgy. Tiguion hills, coordinate at the barangay post for a guide, and hike the short forest trail.
bestTime: Dry morning hours from November to May before afternoon heat builds inside the limestone passages.
tips: Pack a headlamp, closed-toe grippy shoes, and light breathable clothes; several passages connect via low narrow crawls.
photoCredit: Photo: Gerico R. Sapunto · Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

name: St. Joseph Parish Church (1609)
description: Hilltop parish in Barangay II originally founded in 1609, rising above Gasan Centro with grand ramps, warm red-brick masonry, and sweeping views across Tres Reyes Islands.
howToGetThere: Walk 5 minutes uphill from Gasan Municipal Plaza & Public Market along the national coastal highway south of Boac (~25 min by jeepney from Boac).
bestTime: Late afternoon golden hour around 5 PM for sunlit facade photography and ocean sunsets.
tips: Step onto the elevated courtyard balustrade on the seaward side—on clear evenings Tres Reyes Islands silhouette vividly against the western sky.

name: Moriones Festival
description: Marinduque's signature Holy Week Lenten street drama where penitents in hand-carved wooden Roman helmets re-enact the legend of Longinus across Boac, Mogpog (origin town), Gasan, and Santa Cruz. Event pin anchored at Boac Plaza.
howToGetThere: Ferry via Balanacan Port (or Lucena–Buyabod route) into Boac or Mogpog town plazas (~30–40 min by jeepney); processions fill town streets daily.
bestTime: Holy Week annually from Palm Sunday to Easter Sunday (TODO: confirm exact March/April dates for your trip).
tips: Book RORO ferry tickets and homestays weeks ahead for Holy Week—peak processions concentrate around Boac riverbanks and Mogpog Plaza (origin parish).
